summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of kidney transplant, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, coronary artery disease, atrial fibrillation, and peripheral vascular disease, was admitted with persistent diarrhea and abdominal cramping for 12 days. He was found to have a recurrent C. difficile infection, likely triggered by recent antibiotic use during a prior hospitalization. He also presented with acute kidney injury, attributed to dehydration and tacrolimus toxicity, with his level elevated to 11.5. IV fluids were administered, tacrolimus was reduced to 2 mg twice daily, and home diuretics were held. His renal function improved, with creatinine decreasing from 2.8 to 2.0. Atrial fibrillation with rapid rate was managed by transitioning to metoprolol for rate control, then back to carvedilol. His INR was initially elevated at 3.7, prompting temporary discontinuation of warfarin; it was restarted at 1.5 mg daily with a therapeutic INR of 3.2 at discharge. The patient completed initiation of a vancomycin taper for C. diff and was scheduled for a fecal transplant evaluation. He was discharged home with services, on adjusted immunosuppression, anticoagulation, and insulin therapy, with follow-up arranged with transplant, heart failure, and primary care teams.
problems: Enterocolitis due to Clostridium difficile, not specified as recurrent
Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic chronic kidney disease
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease with stage 1 through stage 4 chronic kidney disease, or unspecified chronic kidney disease
